examples.text: China ist ein wichtiger Lieferant für seltene Erden.

glosses: One who supplies; a provider.

examples.text: A farmer could place an order for a new tractor part by text message and pay for it by mobile money-transfer. A supplier many miles away would then take the part to the local matternet station for airborne dispatch via drone.

glosses: Someone who assists (sets up) a goal.

examples.text: Regular supplier Barton played in another teasing corner, which was headed on towards goal by the impressive Ameobi and flicked in by expert poacher Nolan.

translations.source_sense_description: Organisation, die Waren erzeugt und für Kunden bereitstellt

glosses: One who or that which distributes.

examples.text: “The importance of that decision means that the voices of upset consumers have been heard and that those responsible for harming the highly respected reputation of Bud Light and Anheuser-Busch are no longer able to do so,” the distributor said in its statement. glosses: A device that distributes electric current, especially to the spark plugs in an internal combustion engine.

glosses: One who, or that which, provides a service, commodity, or the means for subsistence.

examples.text: In view of this, it is clear why internet service providers (ISPs) are inclined to play a backbench role when it comes to combating file sharing.

glosses: A person or a company that vends or sells.

examples.text: […] Tanee was accosted by certain good fellows, friends and boon companions, who condoled with him on his misfortunes—railed against the queen, and finally dragged him away to an illicit vender of spirits, in whose house the party got gloriously mellow.

glosses: A vending machine.

examples.text: She left her duties guarding the cola vendor and brushed past Earl to the aisle with the creamed corn.

glosses: To bundle third-party dependencies with the source code for one's own program.

examples.text: I distributed my application with a vendored copy of Perl so that it wouldn't use the system copies of Perl where it is installed.

glosses: As the software vendor, to bundle one's own, possibly modified version of dependencies with a standard program.

examples.text: Strawberry Perl contains vendored copies of some CPAN modules, designed to allow them to run on Windows.

examples.text: Un riche propriétaire, M.
